message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it's normal, right?
reply:
**I wouldn’t call this completely normal**, though the rhythm looks regular.

From the image, I see:

- **Sinus rhythm at about 58 beats/minute**, with narrow QRS complexes.
- Relatively tall electrical signals in leads I and aVL, with mild ST–T changes. These can suggest **left ventricular hypertrophy** (thickening of the heart muscle), but ECG voltage alone cannot confirm that. [ECG interpretation reference](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/cardiovascular-disorders/cardiovascular-tests-and-procedures/electrocardiography)
- No obvious acute ST-elevation pattern. That **doesn’t rule out a heart attack**, especially if you have symptoms.

Have a clinician review the original tracing, compare any older ECG, and check your blood pressure. Image interpretation has limits.

**If you currently have chest pain, breathlessness, fainting, or cold sweats, seek emergency care now.**

What prompted the ECG, and are you having any symptoms?
